newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 22.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Friday:
- The Laboratory Corp of America agreed to pay $187 million in civil and criminal penalties to settle federal charges that it billed Medicare for unnecessary blood tests.
- The CompuServe Corp is trying to reinvent itself by building a computer network for home office and small business customers.
- Japanese car drivers are becoming more concerned about the safety of their automobiles.
- Shares of AMR Corp, parent of American Airlines, and Boeing Co have risen this month in anticipation of American's announcement that it will buy jets from Boeing.
- Bell Communications Research Inc, of BellSouth Corp and a number of other companies, has agreed to be acquired by Science Applications International Corp.
- The Securities and Exchange Commission is pressuring companies that pay bribes to disclose the practice or make sure it does not distort financial statements.
- Investors bought $1 billion in Russian bonds as Russia went to the Eurobond market for the first time since before the 1917 Revolution.
- Brazilian state-owned oil company Petrobas said an oilfield off the coast had about 1.3 billion barrels, more than double previous estimates.
- Settlement was reached in the dispute between the direct marketing division of Lowe & Partners/SMS and five former top executives who left unexpectedly to open their own shop.
